area: New-player experience (newplayer): a first run on the frozen 2.1 release, at 1366×768 with a mouse and at 390×844 by touch
summary: A new player reaches the desk about 3 seconds after Clock in plus reading time, and what they read on the way (the three job lines under the memo, 33 words, and the three tour stops, 74 words) correctly teaches the quota, slots against energy and the funnel at both sizes; manager standing, what stress costs and the balance rule are handbook-only at first and then turn up in play when they start to matter, so nothing needs adding to the opening. Seven findings, none in the onboarding sequence itself: the hint bar goes stale under a resting pointer, the handbook hides two rules a newcomer would misread (Collections ends the run; a conference is not lead generation), the idle hint ignores energy, and three terms are never explained where a player meets them (QBR, pp, the quad shot's slot).
verified_ok: Method: a Playwright walk through the frozen release as a brand-new browser, boot screen included, at 1366×768 (mouse) and 390×844 (touch): 54 + 34 pictures, each one cited here was looked at, with the text on screen at every step in d-walk.json, d-walk2.txt, p-walk.json and p-walk2.txt. Everything is in test-results/audit/newplayer/ (file names below are in that folder). The working tree is untouched (git status clean).
Boot (d-01, d-02, p-01): Clock in has the focus, any key or a tap starts it, the sequence runs 2.2 s unskipped and offers Skip; the memo is open 3.0 s after Clock in (timing.cjs).

Memo dialog (d-05, p-05): nothing cut off at either size. On the phone the three job lines (y 555 to 668) and Start week 1 (y 736 to 780 of 844) are on the first screen without scrolling. About 170 words in all, of which the job is 33; with the tour (24 + 24 + 26 words) a player who reads every word is at the desk in about a minute, one who reads only the job lines and the tour in under half that.

First-minute copy against the rules (rules.js, week.js, state.js): quota $160,000, 13 weeks, 5 slots, conferences 2 slots, Recharge needs a slot, salary on Friday, rent in weeks 1, 5 and 9, +15 energy on Friday. Every statement in WELCOME.lines and TOUR is true.

Tour (d-06 to d-08, p-06 to p-08): each stop rings the right control and stays on screen at both sizes, the vendor's ad is held back until it ends, and the focus lands on Prospect blitz with its hint showing. The existing test test/e2e/firstday.cjs, run against the frozen release, passes 27 of 27.

All fourteen hints read on hover at 1366×768 (d-11 to d-24; texts in d-walk.json) and compared with rules.js, actions.js, stress.js and effects.js: prospect 1–4 and a fifth, cadence 0–3, referrals 3% whale, conference 2 slots / 40 energy / $800 / +5 stress / 30% / +8 pp, CRM +5 manager, recharge 35–52 and 12–18, shot 1 +18 / +12 / +13, politics +8 / +3 / −4 / +2, Friday +$1,000 / −$1,600 / +15 / −4. All match.

Concept 1, the objective. Memo dialog, first screen: “Your quota is $160,000. You have 13 weeks.”; the Closed card repeats it as progress (“$0 0% · On pace · Expected by Friday: 0% of quota”). Verdict: learned in the first minute without opening anything. What each result is worth at the end (100% Club, 80–99% kept, 70–79% the review decides, under 70% out) is only in the handbook's first row, which is where it belongs.

Concept 2, slots and energy. Memo dialog: “Each week starts with 5 time slots. Energy is a separate budget.”; tour stop 2: “Most actions use one slot and energy; conferences use two. Recharge restores energy if you have a slot left.”; every card prices itself (“30 energy”) and the Energy card says “+15 on Friday”. Verdict: first minute, and the first week proves it (below).

Concept 3, pipeline progression. Tour stop 1: “Prospect to find leads, qualify them in discovery, demo, propose, then close.”; the board then carries it: the Stage column (Lead, Qualified, Demoed, Proposal, Closing), a count on each funnel card, hints such as “2 leads waiting. Each has a 52% chance to qualify. Trains discovery.” and the idle line “2 leads ready for discovery.” Verdict: first minute.

Concept 4, revenue recognition. Tour stop 1: “A full pipeline is not a full wallet.”; the Deals header (“2 open · $16,722 in pipeline”) sits beside “Closed this quarter $0 0%”; the first signature says the rest: “Close push: 1 signed. $8,182 is no longer a hypothetical. Commission $982.” Verdict: the principle in the first minute; the 12% commission and “not pipeline” in words only in the handbook (“Closed (Q). Closed revenue, net of clawbacks, not pipeline.”, “12% commission on closed sales”) or at the first signature.

Concept 5, manager standing and job security. Not in the memo or the tour (“face the office” is all). What the Manager meter is for is handbook only: “Manager. Approval influences close odds and firing. Email-only weeks cost approval.” (the meter has no tooltip; three hints mention it in passing). That being behind can get you fired is taught by the game itself, in time: the Closed card says “Performance reviews from week 5” from week 3 when behind (x-first-close-hover.png), the log opens week 5 with “Performance reviews begin this week. Please ensure your forecast is visible.” and week 6 with “Behind-pace reviews can now result in termination. HR has cleared its calendar.”, and the card turns to “18 percentage points behind pace” (seeded nine-week beginner run on the test build, naive.cjs). Verdict: handbook only at first, in play by weeks 3 to 6; enough.

Concept 6, stress and rest. On the cards from the first second: “Stress 28 / 100 · Eases 4 on Friday”, “Energy 95 / 100 · +15 on Friday”; tour stops 2 and 3 (Recharge; “recover some energy”); Recharge hint “+35–52 energy, −12–18 stress. Once per week. …”; the quad shot's card “$6 · +25 stress by Friday”. What stress costs is handbook only (“High stress lowers close odds. At 80+ you risk a weekend meltdown; at 100 the run ends immediately”) until the card itself says “Dangerous stress level” at 80 (x-stress-high.png). Verdict: rest in the first minute; the price of stress in the handbook or when it bites.

Concept 7, immediate against future. Nothing explicit in the first minute beyond the tour's wallet line and the card's “Expected by Friday: 0% of quota” (2%, 5%, 10%, 18% in the following weeks: little is expected early). The first Fridays teach it: “A balanced week. For once, the funnel resembles a funnel. +6 pp signing odds next week” (my first Friday), “Parts of your funnel have been declared a nature reserve. −6 pp signing odds next week”, “1 raw lead went stale.” The rule itself is in the handbook (“Full-funnel week. …”). Verdict: by experiment within two Fridays, as the brief wants; the rule only in the handbook (finding 3 is its one inaccuracy).

The first week played as the tour describes it (d-41 to d-56, p-41 to p-56): after three actions energy is 15 with 2 slots left; a blocked press says why (“Proposals. Needs 25 energy. You have 15.”), on the phone as a notice at the bottom of the screen (p-49); Recharge stays lit; “No slots left. End the week.” closes the week.

First Friday and week 2 (d-58, d-60, p-58): the Friday dialog states each option's effect before the choice; the log carries salary, rent and the balanced-week line with their numbers; on the phone the page returns to the top and a notice shows the two lines that matter plus “+3 more in Activity”.

Handbook (d-25, x-handbook-1366-end.png, p-12, x-handbook-390-page2.png, x-handbook-390-page3.png): 550 words on a desktop, 506 on touch (no Keyboard section), 13 px on 19.5 px, readable at both sizes; its rows for the seven concepts agree with the rules; “Read the memo again” reopens the memo. On open it scrolls at 1366×768 (105 px over: the Hail Mary row and the Keyboard section start below the fold), at 1536×864 (9 px) and at 1280×720 (153 px), and fits at 1440×900 with about 29 px to spare (handbook.cjs).

Jargon a newcomer meets, and where it is explained. Explained by use and in reach: quota (memo line and the Closed card), pipeline (tour; Deals header; handbook “Total value of live deals”), discovery, demo, proposal and close (the tour sentence and each card's hint), Hail Mary (its hint, the handbook row, a confirmation on first use), dead leads (the hint counts them), odds (tooltip “Signing chance, conditional on a close attempt”). Never explained in the game: QBR and pp (findings 5 and 6), Collections and the jacket (finding 2), PIP (harmless, see finding 5), SDR (flavour; the copydeck says preserve), CRM, cadence, whale, warm leads, clawbacks, true-up (each guessable from its line; the last two live only in clAInk's own copy). The handbook's term “Closed (Q).” is the card labelled “Closed this quarter”.

Seen and left alone. On touch a hint cannot be read before the tap (deliberate: CHANGELOG, “Hints work by touch”), so a Demo marathon with nothing qualified costs a slot and 28 energy with only the missing count badge and the idle line as cues (x-touch-demo-nothing.png); about one first week in five has Discovery qualify nobody. Tour stop 1's card lies over the Discovery and Close deals cards it names (six cards on the phone). Neither is worth a change at this stage.

findings.title: The hint bar keeps what it said before the press while the pointer (or the focus) stays on the button
findings.where: src/ui/app/ActionGrid.jsx:35-43 and src/ui/app/Foot.jsx:94-105 (the hint is built on mouseenter or focus, and is cleared after a press only on a touch screen); src/ui/app/Board.jsx:18 (it is kept as finished text)
findings.evidence: Frozen release, 1366×768, pointer left where it clicked (stale-hint.cjs). End week in week 4: the desk turns to week 5, the Cash card says “Rent is due Friday”, and the bar still reads “End week. Friday: salary +$1,000, energy +15, stress −4. …” with no rent (test-results/audit/newplayer/x-stale-endweek-w4.png); move away and back and it reads “…salary +$1,000, rent −$1,600, energy +15…”. The reverse from week 1 to 2: the bar keeps “rent −$1,600” while the card says “Rent due in week 5”. So entering weeks 2, 6 and 10 the forecast shows a rent that is not due, and entering weeks 5 and 9 it leaves out the one that is. Recharge: after use the card says “Used this week” and the bar still offers “+35–52 energy, −12–18 stress. Once per week. …” (re-hover: “You have already used this week’s recharge.”). Discovery after the last lead qualified: the bar still says “1 lead waiting. Each has a 85% chance to qualify.” (test-results/audit/newplayer/x-stale-discovery.png; re-hover: “No eligible deals. You would still spend a slot and energy.”), which invites a second press that buys nothing. The same with the keyboard: focus on End week, Enter (stale-focus.cjs). A new player meets it on the first Friday, because End week has just been pressed and the pointer is resting on it. The dashboard audit's folder holds stale-hint-coffee.png and stale-hint-heart-risk.png, so the same cause is probably on file there for the quad shot.
findings.proposal: Rebuild the hint from the run as it stands while a control is under the pointer or has the focus: remember which control the hint belongs to (an action id, end, hail) and call its existing describe() or HINT function again when the run changes, in ActionGrid and Foot or once in Board. No copy changes.
findings.risk: Touch must behave as it does now (the bar returns to the idle line after a tap; a blocked tap's reason stays): test/e2e/phone.cjs:82-96 and test/e2e/confirm.cjs:119 read the bar. The “+N” chip's hint (Foot.jsx:77) has no action behind it and should stay as text.

findings.title: Nothing says that Collections ends the run, and a conference can take you there in one click
findings.where: src/copy/help.js:32 (handbook, Cash); src/copy/ui.js:52 (Cash card) and :96 (Conference hint); src/game/actions.js:222-234 and src/game/deals.js:94-99 (the charge and the ending)
findings.evidence: Every line a player can read about it before it happens: handbook “Collections take the jacket when cash reaches −$1,500 or lower.”; Cash card and log “Collections at −$1,500 cash” (at 1366 px the card breaks it as “Collections at −” / “$1,500 cash”); log “Finance would like to discuss the jacket.”; End week hint “Friday events and collections may change this.” In test-results/audit/strings.json the words for an ending (“ends the run”, “the run ends”, “you are out”) occur only for stress, the quad shot and quota, and nothing explains the jacket before the ending does. Played from a fresh run on the release (conf-path.cjs): Conference, Conference, End week, Recharge, Conference gives “Jacket repo’d. Cash reached −$1,800.” in week 2 (test-results/audit/newplayer/c-04-after-conference-3.png). At −$1,000 the Conference card was lit and its hint unchanged (“3–8 warm leads; some are large. 2 slots, 40 energy, $800, +5 stress. …”), while clAInk's button on the same screen read “Activation unavailable · insufficient cash” (test-results/audit/newplayer/c-03-week-2-hover-conference.png): the vendor's $500 is refused when it would reach the threshold (src/game/claink.js:152), the $800 trip is not, and unlike the fatal quad shot it has neither a hint line nor a confirmation (src/ui/Game.jsx:209-227). The README says it plainly (“Three things end a run early … cash reaching −$1,500”); the game does not.
findings.proposal: Handbook, Cash row: add one sentence after the approved one, “That ends the run.” (help.js's own header says the handbook may not carry a joke that can be misread as a rule; its stress, coffee and quota rows already say “ends the run” or “you are out”.) Optional second step, on the pattern of the quad shot's existing “This shot reaches 100 stress and ends the run.”: when the $800 would take cash to −$1,500 or lower, the Conference hint says so in place of its last sentence.
findings.risk: Adding a sentence leaves the approved one whole, which is what scripts/copy-coverage.mjs looks for; rewording it would open a copydeck row. The handbook has about 29 px to spare at 1440×900 and already scrolls at 1366×768, so one more line makes 1440×900 scroll too. A conditional hint sentence needs a lint fixture (ui.js, lint.params) and must not make the bar three lines: the conference hint is already two at 1366 px.

findings.title: Full-funnel week: a conference is not “lead generation”, and the handbook does not say so
findings.where: src/copy/help.js:36; src/game/week.js:38-53 (lead generation is prospect, cadence or network); src/game/actions.js:218-236 (a conference marks nothing as used)
findings.evidence: Handbook: “Work at least three of four categories (lead generation, discovery, demo, proposal/close) for +6 pp signing odds next week. One or none while holding pipeline gives −6 pp next week.” The Conference hint promises “3–8 warm leads”. On the engine, 400 seeds each (funnel-check.mjs): prospect + discovery + demo earns the bonus 400 times in 400; conference + discovery + demo never; conference + discovery is penalised 400 times in 400. On the release: Conference (4 leads), Discovery (1 qualified), End week gives “Parts of your funnel have been declared a nature reserve. −6 pp signing odds next week” (test-results/audit/newplayer/x-conference-discovery-neglected.png). By the handbook that week touched two categories and should cost nothing. The README words it the same way (“finding leads”).
findings.proposal: Keep the rule. Add one sentence to the Full-funnel row: “Conferences do not count as lead generation.” (or name the three that do: Prospect blitz, Email cadence, Referrals).
findings.risk: None to play. If the omission in week.js is itself the mistake, this documents it instead of fixing it; changing the rule would be a balance change and would move the golden replays. Handbook length as in finding 2.

findings.title: With no energy for it, the idle hint still names the action
findings.where: src/ui/app/Foot.jsx:11-20 (idleHint looks at slots and deals, not energy); src/copy/ui.js:112-120
findings.evidence: The first-week wall, reached by doing what the tour says (Prospect, Discovery, Demo from 95 energy): energy 15, 2 slots left, nine cards dimmed, and the bar reads “2 leads ready for discovery.” though Discovery costs 22 (test-results/audit/newplayer/d-52-after-plan-idle.png). On the phone the same kind of line (“1 demoed deal ready for a proposal.”) is the only guidance there is; tapping the card answers “Proposals. Needs 25 energy. You have 15.” (test-results/audit/newplayer/p-49-after-propose.png). In the seeded beginner run (naive.cjs) every week from 4 to 8 began at 15 to 22 energy, so this is the usual state at the start of a week, not a rare one.
findings.proposal: When the action the idle line names is short of energy, add the sentence the game already has: “2 leads ready for discovery. Needs 22 energy. You have 15.” (HINT.blocked.energy with that action's cost). No new copy.
findings.risk: The line becomes two lines on a phone (the bar reserves two there: src/styles/app.css:258). No test reads the idle line today (grep of test/ and scripts/).

findings.title: QBR is never spelled out in the game
findings.where: src/copy/help.js:29 (“At QBR, 100% earns …”); src/copy/ui.js:19 and src/ui/app/Quarter.jsx:26 (the tag under week 13); src/copy/log.js:85
findings.evidence: test-results/audit/strings.json: “QBR” is in 11 strings, none expands it, and no string contains “quarterly” or “business review”. It labels the week that decides the run (on a desktop; a phone shows no tag: test-results/audit/newplayer/p-43-after-prospect.png) and opens the handbook's first row. The README's “New to tech sales?” list defines QBR, PIP, SDR and CRM, but that list is not in the game. PIP is bare too (“potentially on a PIP”), though with one quarter per run (src/game/constants.js:2) a PIP can only be handed out by the QBR that ends it.
findings.proposal: Handbook, The goal: add “The QBR is the quarterly business review, on the Friday of week 13.” A title on the strip's tag would not reach touch screens.

findings.title: “pp” is never spelled out, and the first Friday can ask for a choice in it
findings.evidence: 19 strings use “pp” (the Conference hint, the status chips, 13 log lines, the handbook, both options of the customer-incident dialog); none says percentage points, while the Closed card (“18 percentage points behind pace”) and the pricing dialog (“+12 percentage points signing odds”) write it out. On my first Friday the dialog asked for a choice between “−15 pp odds for 2 weeks” and “−8 pp odds this week” (test-results/audit/newplayer/d-58-friday-1.png).
findings.proposal: Say it once where the rules are: in the handbook's Full-funnel row, after the approved sentences, “pp: percentage points.” (Writing it out in the incident dialog, as the pricing dialog does, would also work and still fits two lines, but it changes an approved copydeck sentence.)

findings.title: A quad shot takes a slot, and neither its card nor its hint says so
findings.evidence: Card “Quad shot · $6 · +25 stress by Friday”; hint “Shot 1: +18 energy, +12 stress now, +13 more on Friday. Later shots give less and risk more.” (test-results/audit/newplayer/d-21-hover-coffee.png). Pressed with 2 slots left, the strip reads “1 left” (test-results/audit/newplayer/x-coffee-takes-slot.png). The Conference card and hint both list their slots; the tour says “Most actions use one slot” and settles it for Recharge only (“if you have a slot left”); the handbook is the only place that says “Costs cash and a slot”. With one slot left and too little energy, the shot bought for the next action ends the week instead.
findings.proposal: Hint: add “Takes a slot.” after the Friday figure (the Recharge hint could carry the same three words).
findings.risk: The hint goes from one line to two at 1366 px (the bar holds two). The copydeck gives direction for this hint, not fixed wording, so no row opens.

not_checked: Real phones and tablets, Safari and Firefox: Chromium only, and the phone is a 390×844 touch context.
Sound: the announcer's welcome and the memo's cues were not heard (headless); their captions were seen.
Screen readers, and a keyboard-only first run beyond what test/e2e/firstday.cjs asserts.
The first-run flow at tablet sizes and in short windows (under 520 px tall, where the tour scrolls its target to the top); only the handbook was measured at 768×1024.
Reduced motion (the memo without its gag).
Weeks 10 to 13, the QBR and the endings as a new player, and a mid-quarter firing: the seeded beginner run stopped at week 9.

How much of the log the open clAInk ad leaves at 1366×768 (about one entry: d-60-week-2.png). Seen, not assessed: it belongs to the dashboard and clAInk audits and is held by the layout gate (dock-fair).
Whether 2.1.1 work already in hand overlaps these findings: I looked only at the frozen 2.1 build and the committed source.
The lints, the copydeck gate and verify were not run (not allowed). What the proposed sentences would do to them is read from scripts/copy-coverage.mjs and test/engine/copy.test.mjs, not tested.
Comprehension by real newcomers: this is one reader's walk-through, not a playtest.
